title: Before the Waterline
summary: P0 depot calibration and P1 service bridge. Movement, camera and one interaction are taught by doing them; Ivo is met while he is working; Sera is established over radio and the 'current map' question is planted. Ends with Mara crossing into the sealed zone. The 37-minute gap is not mentioned.

objectives.title: Find Ivo in the clinic bay
objectives.description: Ivo Saye runs the field clinic out of the depot's west bay. He asked for a technician, not a courier.

hints.text: The bay is under the departures board, at the west end of the platform.

objectives.title: Read the meter on Feeder Three
objectives.description: The contractor's readout says the transfer to the clinic is clean. Ivo wants a second number from someone who has read a meter before.

hints.text: The meter is mounted beside the bay door, at head height.
Stand square to the panel. The glass is scratched and only reads from the front.

objectives.title: Take the pulse tool from the contractor crate
objectives.description: Holt left a maintenance pulse tool at stanchion four, in the grey case. Nothing in the sealed zone answers a hand signal.

objectives.title: Climb to the upper platform
objectives.description: The service ladder at the east end reaches the upper platform and the head of the service bridge.

hints.text: The ladder is bolted to the lift housing, past the parked bus.

objectives.title: Cross the service bridge into the sealed zone
objectives.description: The north mouth gate lifts by hand. It is rated for two people and there is one of her.

hints.text: The walkway is out for two metres at the mouth. The handrail is not.
Take the strain on the gate slowly, then get under it and through.

objectives.title: Read the evacuation notice board
objectives.description: Three days of amendments in four different hands, over a printed sheet that was current on the first night.

objectives.title: Count the spare batteries on the shelter shelf
objectives.description: Ivo's four includes one that overstates its charge. A written count is worth more to him than his own memory of it.
